name: Zen Lotus Pond
subtitle: Backyard lotus water garden
lede: Filtered, jasmine-flanked lotus water garden with Buddha and simple moving water.
nextAction: Purchase the preferred brown Algreen Manhattan 40-inch Balcony Planter & Pond from Wayfair, then finalize the fish-ready Phase 3 pump and filtration system around its actual setup.
goals: Clean moving water with minimal visible algae and larvae
Start fishless while building circulation and filtration with possible future small fish in mind
Professional compact design framed by jasmine and Buddha
Keep routine maintenance small and predictable

siteConstraints.climate: Very hot summer climate; temperatures can reach about 110°F
siteConstraints.preferredWaterMovement: Gentle bubbler or low fountain to limit evaporation
siteConstraints.maintenanceTarget: A few minutes weekly in hot weather plus roughly 10–15 minutes monthly for filter cleaning as needed
siteConstraints.designIntent: Architectural rectangular pond with open reflective water, lotus and Buddha, framed by jasmine rather than a stock-tank look

phases.name: Lotus Nursery
phases.summary: Establish three seed-grown lotus seedlings in the temporary nursery and keep the water gently moving while they mature.
notes: The $30 Smartpond kit is physically useful with the nursery but is accounted for under Phase 3 equipment and is not included in the $107.13 Phase 1 total.
Some algae in a small sunny nursery is normal; remove visible debris or string algae instead of repeatedly draining and restarting the container.
Keep only a few inches of water above the gravel while the seedlings are young so the leaves can readily reach the surface.

phases.name: Pond Decision
phases.summary: Choose and purchase the permanent pond vessel. The brown Algreen Manhattan 40-inch Balcony Planter & Pond from Wayfair is the preferred choice; purchase is pending.
decisionCriteria: Purpose-built or structurally verified for continuous water load
Enough depth and water volume for lotus stability in extreme summer heat
Straightforward path for pump, mechanical filtration and biological filtration
Reasonable total cost after structure, liner, pump and filter are included

candidates.name: Existing raised planter conversion
candidates.estimatedVolume: Roughly 350–400 gallons operating volume if converted substantially to water
candidates.notes: Earlier option retained for decision history. It would have required verification of framing, cross-bracing, bottom support, liner type/condition, seams, penetrations and patio/slab support before conversion.

candidates.name: Algreen Manhattan 40-inch Balcony Planter & Pond — Brown
candidates.dimensions: 40 in W × 20 in D × 18 in H
candidates.notes: Preferred because the rectangular form fits the architectural design, the brown color has been selected, and the vessel allows Phase 3 filtration to be chosen separately. Not recorded as purchased yet.

candidates.name: Pennington 50-gallon Aquagarden
candidates.notes: All-in-one option considered, but less preferred aesthetically than the Algreen Manhattan.

candidates.name: Separate 4 ft × 2 ft × 2 ft raised pond
candidates.notes: Earlier custom-build option retained as history. If this route ever returns, use a properly framed/braced structural shell with pond-grade underlayment and liner rather than a general-purpose storage tote.

phases.name: Pump + Filter + Fountain
phases.summary: Build the permanent circulation and filtration system so the pond runs fishless now but has enough mechanical and biological capacity for a possible small fish population later without rebuilding the system.
phases.decisionGate: Finalize the main pump/filter after the Phase 2 Manhattan vessel is purchased and the actual plumbing/head layout is known.
requirements: Keep the existing Smartpond kit as the gentle visible fountain and surface-movement feature
Adjustable main pond pump in roughly the 300–500 GPH rated range
Target approximately 200–300 GPH actual flow through filtration after normal flow losses
Mechanical filtration to catch leaves, dirt and dead algae
Biological filtration with generous bio-media capacity sized with possible future fish in mind
Tubing, flow control and a quiet filtered-water return

spendBreakdown.label: Smartpond Filter Kit with Pump from Lowe's

notes: The pond will start fishless, but Phase 3 should be built with future fish-readiness in mind.
UV clarifier is optional and should be added only if persistent free-floating green-water algae becomes a problem.
UV does not solve string algae, wall algae, debris, mosquitoes, worms or odor.
The Smartpond kit is retained for the visible fountain/surface movement; separate mechanical and biological filtration is still required.
Future fish are a later decision and are not part of the initial build.

phases.name: Structure / Liner
phases.summary: Reinforce the pond shell or replace/add pond-grade liner only if the selected permanent pond solution requires it.
notes: This phase could become very small or disappear if a purpose-built pond vessel is selected.
If the existing planter is selected, structural suitability must be confirmed before filling.

phases.name: Jasmine
phases.summary: Frame the pond with two jasmine planters and black trellises using intentionally light foliage density.
phases.layout: Jasmine — Pond — Jasmine, all in the same row
notes: Use two white planters and two black trellises.
Keep jasmine airy rather than creating a dense solid foliage wall.
Provide adequate soil volume and reliable watering for extreme summer heat.

phases.name: Lotus + Buddha
phases.summary: Place lotus on one side, Buddha beside the lotus, fountain toward the opposite side, and preserve open reflective water.
notes: Avoid overfilling the pond visually; open water is part of the serenity goal.
A tiny partially submerged flat stone can be added later for occasional bird drinking if desired, without creating a broad bird-bathing platform.

phases.name: Future State — Fish Ready Prep
phases.timeHorizon: Revisit in about one year after the pond has been established and observed through the seasons.
phases.summary: Brainstorm whether adding a small fish population is appropriate only after the pond proves stable in Arizona conditions. No current purchases or design changes are committed.
notes: Pothos has been removed from the final design; keep the established pond, lotus, Buddha, fountain and jasmine look as-is.
Review real summer water temperatures and oxygen needs before deciding whether fish are appropriate.
Verify the Phase 3 biological filtration has matured and has enough capacity for a small fish load.
If fish are pursued, choose only a conservative number of small fish appropriate for the actual water volume and Arizona heat; no koi.
Decide later whether dedicated aeration, water-testing supplies or other fish-specific equipment are needed before adding fish.

phases.name: Lighting
phases.summary: Add restrained warm accent lighting after the pond system is stable.
notes: Prioritize subtle Buddha and jasmine accent lighting over bright pond-edge lighting.
Primary filtration should use reliable continuous power; decorative lighting can be solar.

decisions.decision: Start fishless. Build Phase 3 fish-ready now, then revisit whether to add a small appropriate fish population in about one year after the pond has proven stable through Arizona conditions.
